blocks.text: “We can no longer wait,” declared Polish victims’ organizations in a dramatic appeal to German civil society, published on November 5 on the website of the Foundation for Polish–German Reconciliation. “Around 50,000 survivors of Nazi persecution during the German occupation still live in Poland today. They include former concentration camp and prison inmates, people deported to Germany for forced labor and those subjected to other forms of Nazi repression,” wrote the signatories of the appeal. The open letter pointed out that many of the survivors are over 90 years old, struggling with illness and rising costs, and in need of help […]...
